newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends down on new trading rules.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends down on new trading rules.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed lower on Tuesday due to Beijing's latest crackdown on trading irregularities, brokers said.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission on Tuesday announced new trading regulations, banning securities rules violators from holding senior positions in the industry or from trading.
The B share index slipped 0.63 points or 0.41 percent to 155.00 on turnover of HK$74.45 million, down from Monday's HK$108.26 million.
"The regulations aimed at reducing speculation dampened sentiment," said an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage.

China will ban company officials and traders from the industry permanently or for several years if they are found to engage in insider trading or price manipulation, the Shenzhen- based Securities Times said on Tuesday.
The rules come into effect immediately.
Shenzhen and Shanghai stock exchanges last Friday also ordered all brokerages to make public each day's five most active stocks and the major traders.

"The market will digest the news before too long," said another analyst. "The index will not fall sharply unless there is other bad news, because investors are generally optimistic about China's 1997 economic outlook.
The A share index reversed early losses to close up 2.05 points or 0.52 percent at 400.27. Turnover was 10.81 billion yuan against 11.12 billion yuan on Monday.
Brokers said they expected the A share index to rise further this week.
"Investors' confidence remains strong despite Beijing's crackdown, especially for listed companies expected to post better 1996 results," said an analyst with China Securities.
On the B share market, China Southern Glass was the biggest loser, down HK$0.15 or 2.96 percent to HK$4.92 on volume of 982,400 shares.
Power supplier Zhuhai Huadian performed strongest on the A share market, surging 0.62 yuan or 10 percent to end limit-up at 6.82 yuan with 6.82 million shares changed hands.
